title: Unit tests for W1-SEATS (seats) (pass 4, sibling imports present, runner tool absent by design)
prompt:
Write the unittest file for `src/minireason/loop/seats.py` — the wave-1 module
W1-SEATS — and make it run green.

There is no test file for this module in the sandbox. Write
`tests/loop/test_seats.py` from the module's own source, its docstrings, and the
acceptance clauses the design of record declares for it. The design entry is in
`design/design-s7-wave-plan.md`; the clauses you must cover are, verbatim:

Two judge seats always carry distinct family labels; selection is a pure byte-stable function of (registry, config); a registry with one family raises FAMILY_COUNT_INSUFFICIENT rather than degrading silently; the gate is multicycle_commitment_study_multi_v2.key_gate imported, not reimplemented, and never admits a sixth concurrent call per key_env; the pins record key_env per seat.

`notes/WAVE0-INTERFACE.md` records the wave-0 interface this module sits on, and
`notes/WAVE1-INTEGRATION-DECISIONS.md` records eight integration decisions the
wave-1 modules are bound by — read both before writing an oracle, because an oracle
that contradicts a decision there is wrong even if it passes.

`docs/examples/test_custody_example.py` and `docs/examples/test_standard_example.py`
are the house style: one behaviour per test, the test name is the sentence the test
asserts, fixtures built in a temp directory, no mocking of the module under test, and
an explicit test per acceptance clause named after that clause. Read them; do not run
them (they assert repository-layout facts this sandbox does not reproduce).

RUN IT:

    python3 run_tests.py tests.loop.test_seats

Iterate until it reports OK. Do not edit `src/minireason/loop/seats.py` or any
other file under `src/` — if a test fails because the module is wrong, leave the test
red and say so in your final message, naming the file, the line and the behaviour;
a failing test that names a real defect is better evidence than a passing suite
bought by weakening the oracle.

A test that asserts only that a name exists, or that re-implements the module's own
computation and compares it to itself, pins nothing. Prefer a constructed input with
a known answer.

Finish by stating, clause by clause, which acceptance clause each test covers, and
which clauses you could not cover and why.

TOOLING. You have read_file, list_dir, grep, write_file and run_command inside a
sandbox. `run_command` accepts only `python3 ...` forms: `python3 -m unittest ...`,
`python3 -m pytest ...`, `python3 -c ...` and `python3 <file.py> ...`. There is no
shell, no `git`, no `ls`, no `cat`, and you cannot set environment variables on a
command line. The sandbox has no network. To run a test module, use the helper that
is already in the sandbox:

    python3 run_tests.py tests.loop.test_<name>

It puts the sandbox root and `src` on `sys.path` and nothing else. You cannot ask
questions; everything you need is in the sandbox.

HOUSE RULES, which hold for every sentence you write.
* No score, no rank, no scalar progress meter, no "better"/"worse" between model
  families, arms, endpoints or modules. Endpoints and arms are independent
  occasions, never competitors.
* A token ceiling, a call budget, a wall clock or a connection close is a RESOURCE
  BOUNDARY. It is never described as exhaustion of the inquiry.
* `unresolved` is a first-class outcome. Say "unresolved", or "I could not
  determine this and here is why", rather than inventing a finding. A finding you
  cannot point at a file and a line for is not a finding.
* Never modify a published observation, and never edit a file to make your own
  claim true.
* Counts are information, never a warrant. Report a count with the command or file
  that produced it beside it.


NOTE FOR THIS RUN: `tools/multicycle_commitment_study_multi_v2.py` is deliberately absent from this sandbox; tests that need the live runner gate must skip with that stated reason, and every other test must run.
evaluation: tests: the file runs green under `python3 run_tests.py tests.loop.test_seats`, a judge counts the acceptance clauses actually covered, and two judge-chosen mutations of the module must each turn at least one test red
